mission.title: Install and Configure Prometheus Operator / kube-prometheus-stack
mission.description: The Prometheus Operator simplifies the deployment and management of Prometheus monitoring stacks on Kubernetes using custom resources. It is ideal for users who want to automate the configuration of Prometheus and related components while maintaining flexibility. Key trade-offs include the need for familiarity with Kubernetes custom resources and potential complexity in advanced configurations.

steps.title: Add the Prometheus Operator Helm repository
steps.description:
This step adds the official Prometheus Operator Helm chart repository to your Helm client.

```bash

helm repo add prometheus-community https://prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts

helm repo update

```

> This repository contains the kube-prometheus-stack chart.
> Updates your local Helm chart repository cache.

steps.title: Install the kube-prometheus-stack
steps.description:
This command installs the kube-prometheus-stack Helm chart in the 'monitoring' namespace, which includes Prometheus, Alertmanager, and Grafana.

```bash

helm install kube-prometheus-stack prometheus-community/kube-prometheus-stack --namespace monitoring --create-namespace --version 0.77.0

```

> Replace '0.77.0' with the desired version if needed.

steps.title: Verify the installation
steps.description:
This step checks if all the components of the kube-prometheus-stack are running correctly.

```bash

kubectl get pods -n monitoring

```

> You should see pods for Prometheus, Alertmanager, and Grafana in the Running state.

steps.title: Access Grafana Dashboard
steps.description:
This command retrieves the Grafana admin password and provides instructions to access the Grafana dashboard.

```bash

kubectl get secret --namespace monitoring kube-prometheus-stack-grafana -o jsonpath="{.data.admin-password}" | base64 --decode; echo

kubectl port-forward svc/kube-prometheus-stack-grafana -n monitoring 3000:80

```

> Use this password to log in to Grafana.
> Access Grafana at http://localhost:3000.

uninstall.title: Uninstall kube-prometheus-stack
uninstall.description:
This command removes the kube-prometheus-stack and all associated resources. Be aware that this will delete all monitoring data.

```bash

helm uninstall kube-prometheus-stack --namespace monitoring

kubectl delete namespace monitoring

```

> This will remove the Helm release.
> This will delete the monitoring namespace and all resources within it.

upgrade.title: Upgrade kube-prometheus-stack
upgrade.description:
Before upgrading, ensure you have a backup of your Prometheus data. This step will upgrade the kube-prometheus-stack to a newer version.

```bash

kubectl cp <prometheus-pod-name>:/prometheus /tmp/prometheus-backup

helm upgrade kube-prometheus-stack prometheus-community/kube-prometheus-stack --namespace monitoring --version 0.77.0

kubectl get pods -n monitoring

```

> Backup Prometheus data.
> Replace '0.77.0' with the desired version.
> Verify that all pods are running after the upgrade.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Error: unable to recognize "": no matches for kind "Prometheus" in version "monitoring.coreos.com/v1"'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that the Prometheus CRD is not installed or not recognized.

**Fix:**
Ensure that the Prometheus Operator is installed correctly and the CRDs are applied.

troubleshooting.title: Grafana dashboard shows 'Data source not found'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This usually means that the Prometheus data source is not configured correctly.

**Fix:**
Check the Grafana data source settings and ensure that the Prometheus service is reachable.

troubleshooting.title: Prometheus pod is in CrashLoopBackOff state
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This can happen due to misconfiguration or resource limits being exceeded.

**Fix:**
Check the logs of the Prometheus pod using 'kubectl logs <prometheus-pod-name> -n monitoring' for more details.

troubleshooting.title: Alertmanager is not sending alerts
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This may occur if the Alertmanager configuration is incorrect or if there are no active alerts.

**Fix:**
Review the Alertmanager configuration and ensure that alerts are defined and firing.
